tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

21	## Résultats principaux
22	
23	1. **Stockage statique (D1).** L'état initial `S3.init statics` porte le stockage statique : ses éléments suivent l'encodage des locaux de `enterFrame`, avec un état initial par feuille. Le cadre 0, qui ne sort jamais, les possède. Pour toute forme statique valide (`ShapeOK 0`), l'état initial satisfait `WF3 ∧ Inv3` (`init_wf`). `Reachable` part de `S3.init statics`, et `StaticPinnedBottom` a maintenant un contenu sur un état atteint (`staticPinned_reached`).
24	2. **Arènes dans `Reachable` (D3).** L'état porte les entrées d'arène. `newArena`, `issue` et `reset` sont des pas de `Reachable`. `reachable_access_invariant_underDD` conclut `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ ∀ ar ∈ s.arenas, s.Active ar.internal → ArenaInv s ar`. Les cas 16 et n4 sont rejoués comme une exécution de `Reachable` depuis `S3.init []`, arène comprise (`case16_reachable`).
25	3. **Forme vide (D2).** `alloc []` est rejeté. Un `alloc` accepté crée toujours une racine (`alloc_ok_new_root`).
26	4. **Ré-ancrage (D4).** À la sortie, une autorité survivante ne change que d'origine, une autorité qui ne survit pas ne change que d'activité. Aucune ne change de mode, d'empreinte ni de détenteur (`exitG_keeps_modes_footprints`). Une autorité `Modify` survivante retire toujours le droit effectif à ses ancêtres survivants (`exit_keeps_restrictions`).
27	5. **Deux demandes ne sont pas réalisables telles qu'écrites.**
28	   - L'arène imbriquée du cas de la tâche, avec un enfant de valeur arène distincte de celle du parent : dans le modèle, l'enfant a toujours la valeur arène du parent (`nested_same_value`). Le module teste la seule forme réalisable. Voir (d) 2 et (e) 2.
29	   - « Le cadre 0 possède exactement les emplacements statiques et leur stockage possédé » : prouvé pour la possession directe. Pour un statique possédé par un autre statique, la possession par le cadre 0 n'est pas invariante (`static_not_owned_by_frame0`). Voir (d) 1 et (e) 1.

/-! ## Arenas in the state (D3) -/

/-- The state with the entry `i` of `arenas` replaced by `ar` (D3). -/
def arenaSet (s : S3) (i : Nat) (ar : Arena) : S3 := { s with arenas := s.arenas.set i ar }

/-- Authority `j` can administer the storage `storage` (D3): active, `Modify`, held by the owner
of `storage`, covering exactly its footprint, and of the kind D3 names: « sa racine si `storage`
est une racine allouée, l'autorité de bloc si `storage` est un bloc émis par une autre arène »,
read by the module as: without origin when `storage` is a root place, derived when it is a part.
D3 says nothing of a part that is not an issued block (pass-5 report, (c) 10 and (e) 6). -/
def IsInternalFor (s : S3) (storage j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧
    OptP (s.P[storage]?) (fun pl => y.holder = pl.owner) False ∧
    (∀ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P storage) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, l ∈ y.footprint) ∧
    (y.origin = none ↔ parentOf s.P storage = none)) False

instance (s : S3) (storage j : Nat) : Decidable (IsInternalFor s storage j) := by
  unfold IsInternalFor; infer_instance

/-- The `internal` of a new arena on `storage` (D3): the first authority that can administer it,
the root of an allocated root, or the block for a storage that is a block of another arena. -/
def arenaInternal (s : S3) (storage : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  (List.range s.A.length).find? fun j => decide (IsInternalFor s storage j)

/-- Preconditions of `newArena storage` (D3), in order: exercisable `Modify` on `storage`;
`storage` usable; `storage` owned by a place, the arena value (A10); no live arena already has
this storage; an authority administers `storage` (`arenaInternal`), which D3 makes the `internal`
of the new arena. -/
def NewArenaPre (s : S3) (storage : Nat) : Prop :=
  HasRight s .modify storage ∧ s.Usable storage ∧ OwnedStorage s storage ∧
    (∀ ar ∈ s.arenas, s.Active ar.internal → ar.storage ≠ storage) ∧
    arenaInternal s storage ≠ none

instance (s : S3) (storage : Nat) : Decidable (NewArenaPre s storage) := by
  unfold NewArenaPre; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `newArena storage` (D3): a new entry, the whole storage available, nothing issued. -/
def newArenaEff (s : S3) (storage : Nat) : S3 :=
  match arenaInternal s storage with
  | some i => { s with arenas := s.arenas ++ [⟨storage, i, s.afp i, []⟩] }
  | none => s

/-- `newArena storage : ok | reject` as a relation (D3). -/
def NewArenaStep (storage : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (NewArenaPre s storage) (newArenaEff s storage)

/-- `arena.issue` on the entry `i` of the state (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3): the step `IssueStep` of the
recorded arena, whose new logical state is written back; a missing entry is rejected. An entry
whose `internal` is released is rejected by `IssueStatic`, which asks it active. -/
inductive IssueAt (k : K) (i via : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (s : S3) :
    AOutcome → Prop where
  | ok {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.ok s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.ok (arenaSet s' i ar'))
  | fail {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.fail s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.fail s)
  | reject {ar : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar → IssueStep k ar via region dst s .reject →
      IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject
  | none : s.arenas[i]? = none → IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject

/-- Preconditions of `arena.reset()` on the entry `i` of the state (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3): the entry
exists and is live (an entry whose `internal` is released cannot be reset), and `ResetPre`. -/
def ResetAtPre (k : K) (s : S3) (i via : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.arenas[i]?) (fun ar => s.Active ar.internal ∧ ResetPre k s ar via) False

## Arbitrages (font foi)
D1. Stockage statique. `S3.init statics`, `statics` au même encodage que les locaux de `enterFrame`, plus l'état initial de chaque feuille (`Init` pour une globale avec initialiseur, `Uninit` sinon). Emplacements possédés par le cadre de base 0, une racine `Modify` par emplacement racine, détenue par le cadre 0. Le cadre 0 ne sort jamais. `StaticPinnedBottom` porte sur ce stockage. Un cadre appelé n'exerce une racine du cadre 0 que par un paramètre dérivé (A2, A3) ; aucune règle d'accès supplémentaire. Le MMIO est représenté comme stockage statique épinglé : les tests vérifient la discipline d'accès, pas la sémantique d'un accès matériel (effets de lecture, modifications externes), qui reste hors du noyau et doit être dite telle dans les docstrings.
D2. `alloc` rejette la forme vide : `shape ≠ []` dans la précondition statique. Une allocation de taille nulle est une forme à une feuille ; sa correspondance avec MM-02 relève du jalon 2.
D3. Arènes dans `Reachable`.
  - L'état porte une liste d'entrées d'arène `{storage, internal}` : `storage` est l'emplacement du stockage administré, `internal` l'autorité qui l'administre. Le propriétaire n'est pas stocké : c'est celui de `storage`, qui suit les transferts (A5).
  - Une arène est vivante ssi `internal` est active. `ArenaInv` est exigé pour toute arène vivante ; une entrée dont `internal` est libérée n'est soumise à rien et ne peut plus servir à `issue` ni `reset`.
  - `newArena storage : ok | reject` enregistre une arène. Préconditions : `Modify` exerçable sur `storage` ; `storage` utilisable ; aucune arène vivante n'a déjà ce stockage. `internal` est l'autorité `Modify` détenue par le propriétaire de `storage` et couvrant exactement son empreinte : sa racine si `storage` est une racine allouée, l'autorité de bloc si `storage` est un bloc émis par une autre arène (arène imbriquée).
  - Arènes imbriquées : l'`internal` de l'enfant est dérivé de celui du parent ; `ResetPre` du parent (aucune autorité active dérivée de son `internal`) refuse donc le `reset` tant que l'enfant vit. Aucune clause supplémentaire.
  - `newArena`, `issue`, `reset` sont des pas de `Reachable`. L'invariant des états atteints devient `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ ∀ ar vivante, ArenaInv s ar`.
D4. Ré-ancrage et exclusivité. Le ré-ancrage ne modifie que `D` et les origines, jamais un mode ni une empreinte (à énoncer : `exitG_keeps_modes_footprints`). Les restrictions d'une autorité dérivée survivante continuent de contraindre ses ancêtres par I1.

## Étapes (un commit par étape)
1. D1 : `S3.init statics` avec états initiaux ; `WF3 ∧ Inv3` sur l'état initial pour toute forme statique valide ; `reachable_access_invariant_underDD` réénoncé depuis `S3.init statics`. `staticPinnedBottom_forces_empty` est remplacé par un témoin où `K.Pinned` est non vide sur un état atteint, où `static_pinned_never_exits` a donc un contenu. `reachable_base_owns_nothing` est réénoncé : le cadre 0 possède exactement les emplacements statiques et leur stockage possédé.
2. D2 : précondition ; témoin `alloc []` → `reject`.
3. D3 : entrées d'arène, `newArena`, `issue`/`reset` dans `Reachable`, invariant étendu ; `reachable_access_invariant_underDD` et `reachable_no_dangling` réénoncés sur le nouveau `Reachable` ; `arena_entry_follows_transfer` (une entrée reste vivante et satisfait `ArenaInv` après le transfert de la valeur propriétaire) ; `arena_dies_with_internal` (après `endUse` de la valeur propriétaire, l'entrée n'est plus vivante).
4. D4 : `exitG_keeps_modes_footprints`.
5. Cas : tous les cas rejoués ; plus :
   - globale `Init` lue par le cadre 0 → `ok` ; globale `Uninit` lue → `reject`, écrite puis lue → `ok` ;
   - globale `Modify` écrite par un appelé sans paramètre → `reject` ; avec un paramètre `Modify` dérivé par l'appelant → `ok` ;
   - région statique épinglée (`K.Pinned`, MMIO) : `transfer` → `reject`, `endUse` → `reject`, lecture et écriture autorisées par la discipline → `ok` (discipline d'accès seulement) ;
   - `alloc []` → `reject` ; `alloc` d'une forme à une feuille → `ok` ;
   - cas 16 et n4 rejoués comme exécutions de `Reachable` depuis `S3.init`, introduction de l'arène comprise (`alloc`, `newArena`, `issue`…), avec une liste d'arènes non vide à chaque état vérifié ;
   - `transfer` de la valeur arène puis `issue` par le nouveau propriétaire → `ok` ; `endUse` de la valeur arène puis `issue` → `reject` ;
   - arène imbriquée : arène enfant sur un bloc de l'arène parent ; `reset` du parent → `reject` tant que l'enfant vit, `ok` après `endUse` de l'enfant et de son bloc ;
   - retour d'une valeur contenant un accès dérivé `Modify` à une partie d'un conteneur de l'appelant ; après le retour, écriture de l'appelant sur tout le conteneur → `reject`, sur une autre partie → `ok` ;
   - retour d'une valeur qui dépend seulement (`D`) d'une partie d'un conteneur, sans accès ; lecture de cette partie par la valeur → `reject` (aucune autorité).

## Hors périmètre
Jalon 2, concurrence, sémantique des accès matériels, handles, `defer`, obligation de libération, syntaxe.

## Règles
Zéro `sorry` ; `#print axioms` au plus {propext, Quot.sound} ; aucun `noncomputable` ; `lake build` sans avertissement ; docstrings citant la clause ou l'arbitrage ; rien d'inventé ; aucun énoncé affaibli, tout changement justifié ; toute propriété non démontrée est signalée, jamais compensée par une précondition ajoutée ; revue adverse ; contre-exemples conservés.

(.ok (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0)])) := .ok (by decide) trivial

/-! ### Cases 16 and n4 as executions of `Reachable` (D3) -/

/-- Case 16 and n4 from the initial state, the arena introduced by `alloc` and `newArena`.
Frame 1: 0 arena value, 1 allocator value, 2 buffer destination. `alloc` gives the storage 3, with
parts 4 and 5, owned by 0, of root authority 3; `newArena 3` registers the arena (entry 0,
`internal` 3). The call passes 4, which observes the arena value, and 5, which modifies the
buffer; the callee local 6 receives the block 7 on the region `[4]`, then is returned to 2. -/
def a0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]
def a1 : S3 := write3Eff a0 [1]
def a2 : S3 := allocEff a1 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0)]
def a3 : S3 := newArenaEff a2 3
def a6 : S3 := enterEff (deriveEff (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) 2 2 .modify) [4, 5] [(none, none, 0)]
def ar7 : Arena := ⟨3, 3, [4, 5], []⟩
def a7 : S3 := arenaSet (issueEff a6 ar7 [4] 6).1 0 (issueEff a6 ar7 [4] 6).2
def a8 : S3 := transferEff a7 6 2
def a9 : S3 := exitEff a8
def a10 : S3 := endUseEff a9 2
def a11 : S3 := resetAtEff a10 0

example : Write3Step 1 [1] a0 (.ok a1) := .ok (by decide)
example : AllocStep KA 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0)] a1 (.ok a2) :=
  .ok (by decide) trivial
example : NewArenaStep 3 a2 (.ok a3) := .ok (by decide)
example : a3.arenas = [ar7] := by decide
example : DeriveStep 0 0 .observe a3 (.ok (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe)) := .ok (by decide)
example : DeriveStep 2 2 .modify (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe)
    (.ok (deriveEff (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) 2 2 .modify)) := .ok (by decide)
example : EnterStep [4, 5] [(none, none, 0)] (deriveEff (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) 2 2 .modify)
    (.ok a6) := .ok (by decide)
example : IssueAt KA 0 4 [4] 6 a6 (.ok a7) := .ok (ar := ar7) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))
example : TransferStep KA 6 2 a7 (.ok a8) := .ok (by decide)
example : ExitStep KA a8 (.ok a9) := .ok (by decide)
example : ResetAtStep KA 0 0 a9 .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : EndUseStep KA 2 a9 (.ok a10) := .ok (by decide)
example : ResetAtStep KA 0 0 a10 (.ok a11) := .ok (by decide)

/-- The run of case 16 and n4 is an execution of `Reachable` from `S3.init []`, and the list of
arenas is not empty from `newArena` on. -/
theorem case16_reachable :
    Reachable KA [] a11 ∧ a3.arenas ≠ [] ∧ a6.arenas ≠ [] ∧ a7.arenas ≠ [] ∧ a8.arenas ≠ [] ∧
      a9.arenas ≠ [] ∧ a10.arenas ≠ [] ∧ a11.arenas ≠ [] := by
  have r0 : Reachable KA [] a0 := .enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))
  have r1 : Reachable KA [] a1 := .write r0 (show Write3Step 1 [1] a0 (.ok a1) from .ok (by decide))
  have r2 : Reachable KA [] a2 := .alloc r1
    (show AllocStep KA 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0)] a1 (.ok a2) from
      .ok (by decide) trivial)
  have r3 : Reachable KA [] a3 := .newArena r2 (show NewArenaStep 3 a2 (.ok a3) from .ok (by decide))
  have r4 : Reachable KA [] (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) :=
    .derive r3 (show DeriveStep 0 0 .observe a3 (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  have r5 : Reachable KA [] (deriveEff (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) 2 2 .modify) :=
    .derive r4 (show DeriveStep 2 2 .modify (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  have r6 : Reachable KA [] a6 := .enter r5
    (show EnterStep [4, 5] [(none, none, 0)] _ (.ok a6) from .ok (by decide))
  have r7 : Reachable KA [] a7 := .issue r6
    (show IssueAt KA 0 4 [4] 6 a6 (.ok a7) from
      .ok (ar := ar7) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)))
  have r8 : Reachable KA [] a8 := .transfer r7 (show TransferStep KA 6 2 a7 (.ok a8) from .ok (by decide))
  have r9 : Reachable KA [] a9 := .exit r8 (show ExitStep KA a8 (.ok a9) from .ok (by decide))
  have r10 : Reachable KA [] a10 := .endUse r9 (show EndUseStep KA 2 a9 (.ok a10) from .ok (by decide))
  exact ⟨.reset r10 (show ResetAtStep KA 0 0 a10 (.ok a11) from .ok (by decide)), by decide,
    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-- Return of a value holding a derived `Modify` access to a part of a container of the caller:
the buffer 2 of case 16 holds the block 7, derived from `internal` on the part 4 of the storage 3.
After the return, a write of the caller on the whole container (expected: reject), on the other
part 5 (expected: `ok`). In the model, a value holds a derived access only as a block issued to
it: `derive` and `split` give the current frame as holder. -/
example : (a9.A[7]?).map (fun y => (y.origin, y.holder, y.footprint, y.mode, y.active)) =
    some (some 3, .place 2, [4], .modify, true) := by decide
example : Write3Step 3 [4, 5] a9 .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : Write3Step 3 [5] a9 (.ok (write3Eff a9 [5])) := .ok (by decide)

/-! ### The arena value transferred or ended (D3) -/

/-- Frame 1: 0 arena value, 1 allocator value, 2 new owner, 3 block destination; `alloc` gives
the storage 4, with parts 5 and 6, owned by 0. After the transfer of the arena value to 2, the new
owner issues a block (expected: `ok`), with `Modify` on the arena value as metadata right (C6).
After `endUse` of the arena value, `issue` is rejected: its `internal` is released. -/
def b0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]
def b1 : S3 := write3Eff (write3Eff b0 [1]) [0]
def b2 : S3 := allocEff b1 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)]
def b3 : S3 := newArenaEff b2 4
def b4 : S3 := transferEff b3 0 2
def arB : Arena := ⟨4, 4, [5, 6], []⟩
example : Write3Step 1 [1] b0 (.ok (write3Eff b0 [1])) := .ok (by decide)
example : Write3Step 0 [0] (write3Eff b0 [1]) (.ok b1) := .ok (by decide)
example : AllocStep K0 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)] b1 (.ok b2) :=
  .ok (by decide) trivial
example : NewArenaStep 4 b2 (.ok b3) := .ok (by decide)
example : b3.arenas = [arB] ∧ arenaValue b3 arB = some 0 := by decide
example : TransferStep K0 0 2 b3 (.ok b4) := .ok (by decide)
example : b4.arenas = [arB] ∧ arenaValue b4 arB = some 2 ∧ b4.Active 4 := by decide
example : IssueAt K0 0 2 [5] 3 b4
    (.ok (arenaSet (issueEff b4 arB [5] 3).1 0 (issueEff b4 arB [5] 3).2)) :=
  .ok (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))
example : EndUseStep K0 2 b4 (.ok (endUseEff b4 2)) := .ok (by decide)
example : ¬ (endUseEff b4 2).Active 4 := by decide
example : IssueAt K0 0 2 [5] 3 (endUseEff b4 2) .reject :=
  .reject (ar := arB) (by decide) (.reject (by decide))

/-! ### Nested arena (D3) -/

/-- An arena nested in a block of another arena, the only form that the model realises: the
`internal` of the child must be held by the owner of its storage (D3), and a block region is
always storage owned by the parent arena value, so the block must be issued to the parent arena
value itself. Frame 1: 0 arena value, 1 allocator value; storage 2 with parts 3 and 4, of root
authority 2; the parent issues the block 3 on `[3]` to 0; `newArena 3` registers the child, of
`internal` 3, derived from
the parent's `internal` 2. The `reset` of the parent is rejected while the child lives; after the
release of the child's `internal`, the child is dead and the `reset` of the parent is accepted. -/
def nA0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]
def nA2 : S3 := allocEff (write3Eff nA0 [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 2, none, 0), (some 2, none, 0)]
def nA3 : S3 := newArenaEff nA2 2
def arP : Arena := ⟨2, 2, [3, 4], []⟩
def nA4 : S3 := arenaSet (issueEff nA3 arP [3] 0).1 0 (issueEff nA3 arP [3] 0).2
def nA5 : S3 := newArenaEff nA4 3
example : NewArenaStep 2 nA2 (.ok nA3) := .ok (by decide)
example : nA3.arenas = [arP] := by decide
example : IssueAt K0 0 0 [3] 0 nA3 (.ok nA4) :=
  .ok (ar := arP) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))
example : NewArenaStep 3 nA4 (.ok nA5) := .ok (by decide)
example : nA5.arenas.map (fun ar => (ar.storage, ar.internal)) = [(2, 2), (3, 3)] ∧
    (nA5.A[3]?).map (·.origin) = some (some 2) := by decide
example : ResetAtStep K0 0 0 nA5 .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : ReleaseStep 3 nA5 (.ok (releaseEff nA5 3)) := .ok (by decide)
example : IssueAt K0 1 0 [3] 4 nA5
    (.ok (arenaSet (issueEff nA5 ⟨3, 3, [3], []⟩ [3] 4).1 1 (issueEff nA5 ⟨3, 3, [3], []⟩ [3] 4).2)) :=
  .ok (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))
example : IssueAt K0 1 0 [3] 4 (releaseEff nA5 3) .reject :=
  .reject (ar := ⟨3, 3, [3], []⟩) (by decide) (.reject (by decide))
example : (releaseEff nA5 3).arenas = nA5.arenas ∧ ¬ (releaseEff nA5 3).Active 3 := by decide
example : ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (releaseEff nA5 3) (.ok (resetAtEff (releaseEff nA5 3) 0)) :=
  .ok (by decide)
theorem nested_reachable : Reachable K0 [] (resetAtEff (releaseEff nA5 3) 0) := by
  have r0 : Reachable K0 [] nA0 := .enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))
  have r1 : Reachable K0 [] (write3Eff nA0 [1]) :=
    .write r0 (show Write3Step 1 [1] nA0 (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  have r2 : Reachable K0 [] nA2 := .alloc r1
    (show AllocStep K0 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 2, none, 0), (some 2, none, 0)] _ (.ok nA2) from
      .ok (by decide) trivial)
  have r3 : Reachable K0 [] nA3 := .newArena r2 (show NewArenaStep 2 nA2 (.ok nA3) from .ok (by decide))
  have r4 : Reachable K0 [] nA4 := .issue r3 (show IssueAt K0 0 0 [3] 0 nA3 (.ok nA4) from
    .ok (ar := arP) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)))
  have r5 : Reachable K0 [] nA5 := .newArena r4 (show NewArenaStep 3 nA4 (.ok nA5) from .ok (by decide))
  have r6 : Reachable K0 [] (releaseEff nA5 3) :=
    .release r5 (show ReleaseStep 3 nA5 (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  exact .reset r6 (show ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (releaseEff nA5 3) (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))

/-- Why the task's form is not realised (pass-5 report, (d) 2): parent and child have the same
arena value 0 (`nested_same_value`), so the `endUse` of the child's value releases both
`internal` (`arena_dies_with_internal`), and the `reset` of the parent is then rejected. -/
example : nA5.arenas.map (arenaValue nA5) = [some 0, some 0] ∧
    EndUseStep K0 0 nA5 (.ok (endUseEff nA5 0)) ∧
    ¬ (endUseEff nA5 0).Active 2 ∧ ¬ (endUseEff nA5 0).Active 3 ∧
    ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (endUseEff nA5 0) .reject :=
  ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide), by decide, by decide, .reject (by decide)⟩

/-! ### Dependency without access -/

/-- Return of a value that only depends (`D`) on a part of a container, without access. Frame 1:
container 0 with parts 1 and 2, result 3; the call passes the authorities 2, which observes the
part 1, and 3, which modifies the result; the callee value 4 depends on 2 and is returned to 3.
After the return, 3 is anchored on the root 0 of the container (A7) and no active authority on the
part 1 is held by 3: the dependency gives no access. A read of the part 1 through the root 1 of
back. -/
def resetAtEff (s : S3) (i : Nat) : S3 :=
  match s.arenas[i]? with
  | some ar => arenaSet (resetEff s ar).1 i (resetEff s ar).2
  | none => s

1:## (c) Décisions non dictées par le texte
16:1. **Ancre effective (C1).** « la racine de sa chaîne d'origines (`RootChain`) » : `S3.effAnchor s x` est le dernier élément de `x :: ancs x`, la chaîne suivie par `RootChain` et le ré-ancrage de A7. Sous l'ordre des origines de `WF3`, elle n'a pas d'origine (`effAnchor_root`). Pour une ancre sans origine, c'est l'ancre elle-même.
17:2. **`EffAnchorOK` sans cas permissif.** `EffAnchorOK s x fd` exige que l'ancre effective existe, que son détenteur ait un cadre, que le dépendant en ait un, et que le premier soit le second ou un de ses ancêtres. `NoEscape` (passe 3) admettait par défaut une ancre sans cadre ou un emplacement sans cadre. L'activité de l'ancre effective n'est pas exigée : C1 n'en parle pas, et I3 porte sur l'ancre elle-même.
18:3. **Clause B8 de `transfer` (C1).** Elle contrôle l'ancre effective quand celle-ci bouge avec la valeur, comme en passe 3, et aussi quand le dépendant bouge : la destination, ou un emplacement que la valeur possède. Sans ce second cas, le `transfer` du cas 10 serait accepté et violerait `AnchorOrder` dans l'état d'arrivée : C1 (« Vaut pour toutes les ancres ») et l'étape 1 (`WF3 ∧ Inv3` sur les états atteints) l'excluent. C'est aussi MM-03.3.6 lu sur l'ancre effective : « Une valeur dépendante ne peut être installée dans une destination dont le cadre survivrait à celui d'une ancre locale dont elle dépend ». La clause découle de `AnchorOrder` de l'état d'arrivée : elle ne rejette que les transferts qui le violeraient. Conséquence : les cas 10 et n9 sont rejetés au `transfer` ((g)).
19:4. **`NoEscape` gardé dans `DependPre` et dans la clause 6 de `TransferPre` (B7).** C1 ne retire pas ces clauses. Pour une ancre sans origine, l'ancre effective est l'ancre elle-même, et `EffAnchorOK` au même cadre implique `NoEscape` ; pour une ancre dérivée, `NoEscape` ne dit rien.
20:5. **`NoDangling` (C2), lu à la lettre.** Pour toute autorité active, tout emplacement non utilisable et toute feuille de son empreinte, l'autorité ne couvre pas cette feuille. L'initialisation n'est pas lue.
21:6. **Hypothèses des préservations.** Chaque préservation d'`AnchorOrder` prend `AnchorOrder s`, et `WF3 s` quand elle en a besoin. Chaque préservation de `NoDangling` prend `NoDangling s`, plus `WF3 s` pour `enterFrame`, `alloc` et `exitFrame`, et `WF3 s` et `Inv3base s` pour `endUse` et `free`. `reachable_access_invariant_underDD` les assemble.
22:7. **`RootsDisjoint` (C3).** Sorti de `WF3`, gardé comme définition et théorème (`rootsDisjoint_always`). Les exemples qui énumèrent les clauses de `WF3` pour `xferCex` et `nd0` le gardent, comme en passe 3.
23:8. **`release` (C4).** Dernière clause de `ReleasePre` : l'autorité a une origine, et son détenteur est le cadre courant ou un emplacement `p` avec `HasRight s .modify p`. `HasRight` est le droit `Modify` exerçable de B2, déjà demandé par `transfer`, `endUse` et `free`. La disjonction de la passe 3 (« exerçable à un mode ») disparaît.
24:9. **`endUse` (C5, C8).** Dernière clause de `EndUsePre` : aucune feuille finissante épinglée, statiquement ou dynamiquement, quel que soit `ExternalDone`. `endUseS` marque mortes les places possédées par `p` ou une de ses parties, jamais `p` : déjà conforme à C8, aucune correction. Cas de la passe 4 : un local fini puis réécrit et relu.
25:10. **`StaticPinnedBottom` (C5).** « toute feuille couverte par `K.Pinned` appartient à un emplacement possédé, transitivement, par le cadre de base » : `∀ l, K.Pinned l → ∃ q, l ∈ footprint s.P q ∧ OwnedByFrame s.P (s.F.getLastD 0) q`. Le cadre de base est le dernier de la pile, que la sortie ne retire jamais. Sous `WF3`, tous les emplacements qui contiennent une feuille ont le même propriétaire : la forme existentielle équivaut à la forme universelle. Hypothèse nommée de `static_pinned_never_exits` et du témoin `staticPinnedBottom_forces_empty`.
26:11. **`static_pinned_never_exits`.** Pour un état `WF3` de pile `f :: F₀` avec `F₀ ≠ []`, sous `StaticPinnedBottom` : un emplacement utilisable avant la sortie et plus après ne couvre aucune feuille de `K.Pinned`. C'est la partie statique de la clause B4 de `ExitPre`.
27:12. **Forme de `alloc` (C6).** `List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)`, comme les locaux de `enterFrame` : parent, élément propriétaire, `kind`, en indices absolus.
32:13. **Métadonnées du fournisseur (C6).** Ce sont les feuilles du fournisseur, celles sur lesquelles `ProviderRight` (B5) donne le droit de mise à jour. `AllocStatic` exige qu'elles soient toutes `Init` ; l'effet les met à `Init`, comme `issue` pour l'arène. Sous la précondition, cette écriture ne change pas `I`.
33:14. **`Satisfiable` (C9).** `K.Satisfiable provider shape s`, lu dans l'état avant `alloc`. Ordre des issues inchangé : `reject` si une précondition statique échoue, sinon `fail` si `Satisfiable` est faux, sinon `ok`. Aucun théorème ne le suppose vrai.
34:15. **`MetaRight` (C6).** Premier disjoint ajouté : `Modify` exerçable sur la valeur arène (`OptP (arenaValue s ar) (HasRight s .modify) False`). `ResetPre` lit le même `MetaRight` depuis la passe 2 : l'alignement vaut aussi pour `reset`.
35:16. **Théorèmes de la passe 3 sur `alloc`.** `alloc_fresh` est généralisé à tous les indices nouveaux. `alloc_owned_root` est énoncé par élément racine ; sa clause « l'empreinte est l'emplacement lui-même », propre à une feuille, passe dans `alloc_owned_root_leaf`, qui reprend mot pour mot les conjoints de la passe 3 pour la forme `[(none, none, 0)]`.
36:17. **Forme vide.** `ShapeOK n []` vaut et aucune précondition ne l'exclut : `alloc` de `[]` est `ok`, sans emplacement ni autorité. Question (e) 2.
37:18. **Témoins sans `WF3`.** Le témoin de `transfer_not_inv3_preserving` en passe 3 ancrait la place 2 sur l'autorité 5, qui n'existe pas. Sous la clause B8 de C1, son `transfer` est rejeté : `EffAnchorOK` exige que l'ancre effective existe. L'étape 1 l'a donc ré-ancré sur une racine 2 libérée, ajoutée à `A`. Cet état viole `NoDangling` (étape 2). Il reste en `example` sous le nom `xferNd`, avec `¬ NoDangling xferNd`. `transfer_not_inv3_preserving` garde son énoncé de la passe 3 sur un nouveau `xferCex`, qui satisfait l'`Inv3` complet : la source a un lien de parent vers un emplacement d'indice supérieur, que `chain` ignore, si bien qu'elle ne couvre aucune feuille. Le témoin de `alloc_not_inv3_preserving` a ses feuilles `Init`, comme C6 l'exige du fournisseur.
39:## (d) Théorèmes non prouvés tels que demandés, et pourquoi
41:1. **`static_pinned_never_exits`** est prouvé, sous `WF3` et `StaticPinnedBottom`. Sur un état atteint, l'hypothèse force `K.Pinned` vide (`staticPinnedBottom_forces_empty`), et la conclusion est alors triviale. Question (e) 1.
42:2. **Inchangés depuis la passe 3** : passe 2, (d) 2 (`DDSound` nécessaire), 3 (`Reachable` sans `issue` ni `reset`) et 6 (pas de totalité).
43:3. **Théorèmes qui réénoncent une précondition** (passe 2, (d) 5 ; passe 3, (d) 4). Inchangés ; `alloc_fail_unchanged` lit maintenant `Satisfiable pr ls s`.
47:## (e) Questions pour arbitrage
53:1. **`StaticPinnedBottom` sur les états atteints** ((c) 10, (d) 1). L'état initial a un cadre et aucun emplacement (brief de la passe 1 : « un cadre, aucun emplacement »). `enterFrame` donne à ses locaux le nouveau cadre ou un emplacement pour propriétaire, `alloc` et `transfer` un emplacement. Le cadre de base, 0, ne possède donc jamais rien (`reachable_base_owns_nothing`). Sur un état atteint, `StaticPinnedBottom k s` équivaut à `K.Pinned` vide (`staticPinnedBottom_forces_empty`). Lire « cadre de base » comme le premier cadre entré ne marche pas : ce cadre peut sortir. Dans `c13a`, de pile `[1, 0]`, le local 0 appartient au cadre 1 et meurt à sa sortie (exemple de la section des témoins) ; avec `K.Pinned = {0}`, le théorème serait faux. Faut-il :
57:2. **Forme vide de `alloc`** ((c) 17). B5 : « `ok` : nouvelle racine d'identité fraîche ». C6 donne à la forme l'encodage des locaux de `enterFrame`, qui admet la liste vide. `alloc` de `[]` est aujourd'hui `ok` sans effet sur `P` ni `A`. Faut-il la rejeter, ou l'accepter telle quelle ?

import Ern.MM03
namespace Ern.MM03

def y0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]
def y1 : S3 := write3Eff y0 [1]
-- root 4 with single part 5: footprint 4 = footprint 5 = [5]
def y2 : S3 := allocEff y1 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)]
example : footprint y2.P 4 = [5] ∧ footprint y2.P 5 = [5] := by decide
def y3 : S3 := newArenaEff y2 4
example : NewArenaStep 4 y2 (.ok y3) := .ok (by decide)
-- second arena on the part 5 (same leaves), no block involved: accepted, same internal 4
def y4 : S3 := newArenaEff y3 5
example : NewArenaStep 5 y3 (.ok y4) := .ok (by decide)
example : y4.arenas.map (fun ar => (ar.storage, ar.internal, ar.available)) = [(4, 4, [5]), (5, 4, [5])] ∧
    y4.Active 4 := by decide
theorem w2_reachable : Reachable K0 [] y4 :=
  .newArena (.newArena (.alloc (.write (.enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide)))
    (show Write3Step 1 [1] y0 (.ok y1) from .ok (by decide)))
    (show AllocStep K0 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)] y1 (.ok y2) from .ok (by decide) trivial))
    (show NewArenaStep 4 y2 (.ok y3) from .ok (by decide)))
    (show NewArenaStep 5 y3 (.ok y4) from .ok (by decide))
-- both live entries issue the same leaf: first ok, second rejected by the access discipline
def y5 : S3 := arenaSet (issueEff y4 ⟨4, 4, [5], []⟩ [5] 2).1 0 (issueEff y4 ⟨4, 4, [5], []⟩ [5] 2).2
example : IssueAt K0 0 0 [5] 2 y4 (.ok y5) := .ok (ar := ⟨4, 4, [5], []⟩) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))
example : IssueAt K0 1 0 [5] 3 y5 .reject := .reject (ar := ⟨5, 4, [5], []⟩) (by decide) (.noRight (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))
#print axioms w2_reachable

/- (7): any two places sharing a leaf have the same owner under WF3 (WF3.ownerOf), so a child
   arena whose storage shares a leaf with the parent storage has the parent's arena value. -/
theorem shared_leaf_same_owner {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {q₁ q₂ l : Nat}
    (h₁ : l ∈ footprint s.P q₁) (h₂ : l ∈ footprint s.P q₂) :
    (s.P[q₁]?).map (·.owner) = (s.P[q₂]?).map (·.owner) := by
  have p₁ : partOf s.P l q₁ := (of_decide_eq_true (List.mem_filter.1 h₁).2).2
  have p₂ : partOf s.P l q₂ := (of_decide_eq_true (List.mem_filter.1 h₂).2).2
  obtain ⟨pl, pr, hl, hr, he⟩ := hw.ownerOf p₁
  obtain ⟨pl', pr', hl', hr', he'⟩ := hw.ownerOf p₂
  rw [hl] at hl'; cases hl'
  rw [hr, hr']; simp [← he, he']

theorem nested_same_value {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {par child : Arena} {l : Nat}
    (h₁ : l ∈ footprint s.P par.storage) (h₂ : l ∈ footprint s.P child.storage) :
    arenaValue s par = arenaValue s child := by
  have := shared_leaf_same_owner hw h₁ h₂
  unfold arenaValue
  cases hp : s.P[par.storage]? <;> cases hc : s.P[child.storage]? <;> rw [hp, hc] at this <;>
    simp at this <;> simp [this]
#print axioms nested_same_value
end Ern.MM03

findings.evidence: Report line 213: « rejeter `newArena` sur un stockage qui n'est ni une racine allouée ni un bloc émis, comme le fait le module ». The report contradicts this itself in two places. Line 55 says « Le module étend ces deux cas : sans origine pour un emplacement racine, dérivée pour une partie ». Line 160 says « Le module les lit comme « emplacement racine » (autorité sans origine) ». In the module, `IsInternalFor` requires only `y.origin = none ↔ parentOf s.P storage = none`. So any root place owned by a place, whose root authority is held by its owner, is accepted, allocated or not. Lean check (scratchpad/rev12/newclaims/c2.lean, run with `lake env lean`): the only error is on an unrelated helper line, and all of the following are accepted. (1) A static owned by another static: `Reachable K0 stO (S3.init stO)` and `NewArenaStep 1 (S3.init stO) (.ok (newArenaEff (S3.init stO) 1))`, with `arenaInternal (S3.init stO) 1 = some 1` (#eval). Storage 1 is a static, not an `alloc` root and not a block. (2) A local owned by another local: with `def lo : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, some 0, 0)]`, `Reachable K0 [] lo`, `NewArenaStep 1 lo (.ok (newArenaEff lo 1))` and `(newArenaEff lo 1).arenas.map (fun ar => (ar.storage, ar.internal)) = [(1, 1)]` all hold. So the status quo offered to the arbiter as option 1 misdescribes the module. Only the restriction on parts (« Le module exige une autorité dérivée pour toute partie », line 212) matches what the module does.
findings.suggested_fix: In (e) 6, first option, replace « rejeter `newArena` sur un stockage qui n'est ni une racine allouée ni un bloc émis, comme le fait le module ; » with « rejeter `newArena` sur une partie qui n'est pas administrée par une autorité dérivée, comme le fait le module (pour un emplacement racine, le module accepte sa racine, que l'emplacement soit alloué, statique ou local) ; ».
